newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican corn farmers eye physical market for May.
newsitem.headline: Mexican corn farmers eye physical market for May.

text.p: Mexican corn farmers from the northeastern state of Sinaloa will set up a physical market to trade corn by May this year, the state-owned news agency Notimex said Monday.

Citing Luis Antonio Cardenas Fonseca, the chairman of the Confederation of Sinaloa Farm Associations, Notimex said the state's farmers hoped to trade most of its annual production of 2.5 million tonnes via the market.
Cardenas Fonseca said the market would sell corn stored in warehouses and backed by certificates of deposit. He said the government's staples agency Conasupo would buy via the market.
Mexico currently has no formal physical agricultural exchanges to trade products, although various states and farm groups are bidding to establish them.
The only markets are wholesale outlets in major cities providing produce to buyers such as supermarket chains.
No details of where the market would be based were given, although Cardenas Fonseca said it would first trade white corn grown in Mexico and then add other grains.
The farm leader said exports to South Africa and Central America were anticipated from the start-up of the market, but only in small volumes.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
